_comment: Tier-2 for skfem heat_transient#0, verified 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1. Claim: backward Euler is unconditionally stable but only first order, signalled by the L-infinity error decreasing by ~2 per dt halving instead of ~4. Ran: u_t = Laplace u on MeshTri.init_tensor 20x20 with ElementTriP1 (441 DOFs, 361 interior), homogeneous Dirichlet, IC sin(pi x) sin(pi y), T = 0.02, 4/8/16/32/64 steps for theta = 1 and theta = 0.5, errors as max|u_h - u_ref| over interior DOFs against a 1024-step SAME-MESH reference (against the analytic solution the spatial error saturates and the study is meaningless). Printed: backward Euler reduction factors 1.955/1.988/2.018/2.059, slopes 0.967/0.992/1.013/1.042; Crank-Nicolson on the same mesh gives 4.101/4.002/4.003/4.012, slopes ~2, so the entry's 2-vs-4 discriminator works and the two schemes never overlap. Unconditional stability checked separately: a single step covering the whole interval stays finite and decays to 0.718651. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 raises be_theta, the theta of the 'be' sweep, from 1.0 to 0.5, i.e. replaces backward Euler by the second-order scheme this entry's own discriminator points at; the unconditional-stability probe stays at theta = 1.0 because it is a property of backward Euler, not the pathology. Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1: the unmutated run matches all 9 expect_in_output strings; T2_MUTATE=1 removes 'be_factor_is_about_two=True', 'be_slope_is_one=True', 'be_factor_is_about_four=False' and 'the_two_schemes_are_distinguishable=True' so the fixture goes red. Re-run: T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py
